name.text: Compound arguments: solving cos(nθ) = b for 0° ≤ θ ≤ 360°

questiontext.text:
Solve the equation

\[ {@c@}\cos\left([[if test="is(n=1/2)"]]\dfrac{\theta}{2}[[else]]{@n@}\theta[[/if]]\right) = {@rhs@} \qquad\text{for } 0^\circ \le \theta \le 360^\circ. \]

Use the substitution \(u = [[if test="is(n=1/2)"]]\dfrac{\theta}{2}[[else]]{@n@}\theta[[/if]]\). Give angles in degrees; use a decimal where needed. Type a list of solutions like [30, 150], in any order.

(a) Since \(0^\circ \le \theta \le 360^\circ\), find the range of values of \(u\).

\(0^\circ \le u \le \) [[input:ans_umax]]\(^\circ\) [[validation:ans_umax]] [[feedback:prta]]

(b) Solve the equation for \(u\), giving all the solutions in this range.

\(u = \) [[input:ans_u]] [[validation:ans_u]] [[feedback:prtb]]

(c) Hence find all the solutions for \(\theta\) with \(0^\circ \le \theta \le 360^\circ\).

\(\theta = \) [[input:ans_t]] [[validation:ans_t]] [[feedback:prtc]]

generalfeedback.text:
Worked solution

We solve \({@c@}\cos\left([[if test="is(n=1/2)"]]\dfrac{\theta}{2}[[else]]{@n@}\theta[[/if]]\right) = {@rhs@}\) for \(0^\circ \le \theta \le 360^\circ\) using the substitution \(u = [[if test="is(n=1/2)"]]\dfrac{\theta}{2}[[else]]{@n@}\theta[[/if]]\).

(a) The range of \(u\)

[[if test="is(n=1/2)"]]Since \(u = \dfrac{\theta}{2}\), halve both ends of the range of \(\theta\)[[else]]Since \(u = {@n@}\theta\), multiply both ends of the range of \(\theta\) by \({@n@}\)[[/if]]:

\[ 0^\circ \le \theta \le 360^\circ \quad\Longrightarrow\quad 0^\circ \le u \le {@umax@}^\circ. \]

[[if test="is(n>1)"]]So \(u\) goes round the unit circle \({@n@}\) times, and we must look for solutions in every one of those turns.[[else]]So \(u\) only goes half-way round the unit circle, and some solutions of \(\cos u = {@k@}\) will be outside this range.[[/if]]

(b) Solving for \(u\)

Step 1: get \(\cos u\) on its own. Divide both sides by \({@c@}\): \(\cos u = \dfrac{ {@rhs@} }{ {@c@} } = {@k@}\).

Step 2: find the solutions in the first turn, \(0^\circ \le u \le 360^\circ\). From the special triangles, \(\cos^{-1}\left({@k@}\right) = {@beta@}^\circ\). Cosine is symmetric about \(180^\circ\), so the other solution in the first turn is \(360^\circ - {@beta@}^\circ = {@360-beta@}^\circ\).

Step 3: use the full range of \(u\). [[if test="is(n=1/2)"]]The range is only \(0^\circ \le u \le 180^\circ\), so \({@360-beta@}^\circ\) is outside it and is rejected. The only solution is \(u = {@beta@}^\circ\).[[/if]] [[if test="is(n=2)"]]The range goes up to \(720^\circ\), so add \(360^\circ\) to each first-turn solution: \({@beta@}^\circ + 360^\circ = {@360+beta@}^\circ\) and \({@360-beta@}^\circ + 360^\circ = {@720-beta@}^\circ\). Adding another \(360^\circ\) would go past \(720^\circ\).[[/if]] [[if test="is(n=3)"]]The range goes up to \(1080^\circ\), so add \(360^\circ\) and then \(720^\circ\) to each first-turn solution: this gives \({@360+beta@}^\circ\), \({@720-beta@}^\circ\), \({@720+beta@}^\circ\) and \({@1080-beta@}^\circ\).[[/if]] So

\[ u = {@solsU@} \qquad (\text{{@nsol@} solution[[if test="is(nsol>1)"]]s[[/if]]}). \]

(c) Converting back to \(\theta\)

[[if test="is(n=1/2)"]]Since \(u = \dfrac{\theta}{2}\), we have \(\theta = 2u\): multiply each solution by \(2\)[[else]]Since \(u = {@n@}\theta\), we have \(\theta = \dfrac{u}{ {@n@} }\): divide each solution by \({@n@}\)[[/if]]:

\[ \theta = {@solsT_disp@}. \]

Every value lies in \(0^\circ \le \theta \le 360^\circ\), as it must, because we used the matching range for \(u\). The graph of \(y = \cos\left([[if test="is(n=1/2)"]]\dfrac{\theta}{2}[[else]]{@n@}\theta[[/if]]\right)\) shows why there [[if test="is(nsol>1)"]]are {@nsol@} solutions: the curve repeats {@n@} times between \(0^\circ\) and \(360^\circ\)[[else]]is only one solution: the curve only completes half a cycle between \(0^\circ\) and \(360^\circ\)[[/if]].

questiondescription.text: Objective: solve trigonometric equations with a compound argument (Type 1), using the substitution u = nθ, the adjusted range of u, all solutions in that range, and conversion back to θ.

prtcorrect.text: Correct answer, well done.

prtpartiallycorrect.text: Your answer is partially correct.

prtincorrect.text: Incorrect answer.

node.description: Divided instead of multiplied (or the reverse)

truefeedback.text: Check the direction. [[if test="is(n=1/2)"]]\(u = \dfrac{\theta}{2}\), so halve the ends of the range of \(\theta\).[[else]]\(u = {@n@}\theta\), so multiply the ends of the range of \(\theta\) by \({@n@}\).[[/if]]

falsefeedback.text: Replace \(\theta\) by its largest value, \(360^\circ\), in the expression for \(u\).

node.description: Only the first-turn solutions (range goes beyond 360)

truefeedback.text: Those are the solutions in the first turn, \(0^\circ \le u \le 360^\circ\), but \(u\) goes up to \({@umax@}^\circ\). Add \(360^\circ\) to each solution[[if test="is(n=3)"]], and then \(720^\circ\),[[/if]] to find the solutions in the other turns.

node.description: Included a solution outside the range of u

truefeedback.text: One of your values is outside the range of \(u\), which only goes up to \({@umax@}^\circ\). Reject any solution that is larger than that.

node.description: Solutions for the opposite sign of cos u

truefeedback.text: Those angles solve \(\cos u = {@-k@}\), not \(\cos u = {@k@}\). Check the sign after dividing by \({@c@}\), and use the CAST rule.

falsefeedback.text: Divide by \({@c@}\) to get \(\cos u\) on its own. Find \(\cos^{-1}\) of that value and the matching angle \(360^\circ\) minus it, then add or remove multiples of \(360^\circ\) to list every solution between \(0^\circ\) and \({@umax@}^\circ\).

node.description: Correct conversion of the student's own (b)

truefeedback.text: You have converted your values of \(u\) from part (b) correctly, but your part (b) is not right. Correct it first, then convert again.

node.description: Gave the u values, not converted

truefeedback.text: These are the solutions for \(u\). You still need to convert them back to \(\theta\) using [[if test="is(n=1/2)"]]\(\theta = 2u\)[[else]]\(\theta = \dfrac{u}{ {@n@} }\)[[/if]].

You have converted the wrong way. [[if test="is(n=1/2)"]]\(u = \dfrac{\theta}{2}\), so \(\theta = 2u\): multiply by \(2\).[[else]]\(u = {@n@}\theta\), so \(\theta = \dfrac{u}{ {@n@} }\): divide by \({@n@}\).[[/if]]

falsefeedback.text: Convert each solution for \(u\) from part (b) back to \(\theta\). Every value of \(\theta\) should lie between \(0^\circ\) and \(360^\circ\).
